title: TSMC to develop site in Baipu park
gist: TSMC is building a 3-hectare advanced-packaging validation and training site in Kaohsiung's Baipu Industrial Park, expecting CoWoS-type packaging capacity to grow at over 80% CAGR through 2029, while Taiwan's semiconductor trade body projects industry revenue near $300 billion this year (+40% YoY) and SEMI's CEO sees the global chip market reaching $2 trillion by 2030.

insights.claim: TSMC is developing a 3-hectare site in Kaohsiung's Baipu Industrial Park, in partnership with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Kaohsiung City Government, to accelerate testing and validation of semiconductor materials and equipment.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A dedicated validation/training campus signals TSMC is institutionalizing advanced-packaging capacity build-out as a long-term core competency, not just a temporary AI-cycle response — relevant to suppliers of packaging materials and equipment seeking co-location.
insights.locator: opening paragraphs, TSMC vice president Jun He remarks

insights.claim: TSMC vice president of advanced packaging technology and service Jun He said the Baipu site is expected to improve validation efficiency by 25 to 50 percent.
insights.speaker: Jun He (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A quantified efficiency gain on validation cycles implies faster iteration on new packaging processes, which could compress time-to-qualification for next-gen CoWoS/SoIC variants and give TSMC a process-speed edge over Intel Foundry and Samsung Foundry.
insights.locator: second paragraph, at the 3D IC global summit

insights.claim: The Baipu site will include two modular buildings with small clean rooms and laboratories, designed to be reconfigured as technology evolves, aiming to build a world-class training base for advanced-packaging talent and connect local suppliers to global supply chains.
insights.speaker: Jun He (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Modular, reconfigurable facility design plus an explicit talent-training mandate signals TSMC is trying to solve the packaging-skills bottleneck structurally, not just add floor space — a leading indicator of sustained hiring/training investment in Taiwan's supply base.
insights.locator: mid-article, description of the planned facilities

insights.claim: TSMC expects its chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging capacity to grow at a compound annual growth rate of more than 80 percent through next year (2027), with growth expected to remain robust through 2029.
insights.speaker: Jun He (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: An >80% CAGR guide for CoWoS capacity through 2027 (and continued robust growth to 2029) is a concrete capex/demand data point for tracking TSMC's advanced-packaging revenue trajectory and downstream HBM/interposer supplier order books (e.g., SK Hynix, Samsung, Amkor).

insights.claim: Taiwan Semiconductor Industry Association president Wu Chih-i said Taiwan's semiconductor industry revenue is projected to be close to US$300 billion this year, more than 40 percent growth over last year, driven by AI demand.
insights.speaker: Wu Chih-i (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A ~40% YoY national semiconductor revenue growth figure is a macro proxy for AI-chip demand intensity flowing through the entire Taiwan supply chain, useful for cross-checking TSMC/MediaTek/ASE segment guidance.
insights.quote: This year Taiwan’s semiconductor industry has performed even better. Our total revenue is projected to be close to US$300 billion. That’s more than 40 percent growth over last year
insights.locator: quote from Wu Chih-i at Semicon Taiwan opening

insights.claim: Wu Chih-i warned that energy supply, talent and cybersecurity are becoming more critical constraints for the industry, and that no single country can dominate the chip supply chain, arguing for closer international semiconductor collaboration.
insights.speaker: Wu Chih-i (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: Industry leadership publicly flagging energy, talent and cybersecurity as binding constraints (not just capex or equipment) points investors toward power-infrastructure and workforce-training plays as second-order beneficiaries of the AI chip buildout.
insights.quote: Continuous progress will require even closer semiconductor collaboration between many countries
insights.locator: quote from Wu Chih-i on industry constraints

insights.claim: SEMI president and CEO Ajit Manocha said global semiconductor revenue could reach US$2 trillion by 2030 as AI shifts from training to inference, driving demand for memory, higher bandwidth, advanced packaging and silicon photonics.
insights.speaker: Ajit Manocha (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A $2 trillion by 2030 industry forecast anchored to the training-to-inference shift gives investors a top-down sizing benchmark and flags memory, packaging and photonics as the specific sub-sectors expected to capture incremental spend.
insights.locator: near end of article, Manocha's global forecast

insights.claim: Manocha characterized the current period as "the decade of AI" but cautioned the industry is in the "early innings" and will face significant headwinds, describing the path forward as not a straight line.
insights.speaker: Ajit Manocha (via SemiWiki)
insights.so_what: A top industry-association executive explicitly tempering an otherwise bullish decade-long AI growth thesis with an 'early innings, not a straight line' caveat is a useful hedging signal against overextrapolating current capex growth rates.
insights.quote: It's not going to be a straight line. We're going to have to learn how to deal with and navigate through the new opportunities and new headwinds.
